title: fix: disable auto top-up after the first declined payment
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Stops the repeated-charge loop by disabling auto top-up after the first declined payment. Customers can re-enable it without a cooldown. This deliberately reverses [fba6917016](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations/commit/fba69170166cb7fc77968c3c815b91c1462d6921), which kept auto top-up enabled after payment failure; the investigation found five accounts caused 98% of 7,158 failures.
- Shows “Off — last charge failed” on the Pollen page, with guidance to check the payment method and re-enable auto top-up.
- Records the failure and disables auto top-up atomically. Handles void-before-decline delivery and duplicate webhooks without undoing a customer’s later decision to re-enable it. Removes an unused database return value.
- Preserves pending 3DS authentication and already-paid attempts. Voided and uncollectible invoices alone do not disable auto top-up.
- Validation: 79/79 Stripe integration tests, TypeScript, Biome, and frontend build pass. Radar-blocked payment webhook delivery has not been verified in the Stripe sandbox.

gist.headline: One decline, then a pause
gist.blurb: Auto top-up now pauses after a declined charge instead of trying again and again. Check your payment method, then turn it back on whenever you're ready.
gist.summary: Auto top-up now switches off after the first declined payment, records the failure atomically, and shows “Off — last charge failed” on the Pollen page; customers can re-enable it without a cooldown.
gist.impact: A declined charge no longer triggers repeated auto top-up attempts, while pending 3DS authentication and already-paid attempts continue unaffected.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the Pollen page as a cozy pixel-art billing desk: Polli gently moves an auto top-up switch to Off beside a declined payment card, with a clear path to switch it back on. A small flower pot of Pollen coins keeps the scene warm rather than alarming.
